POLICY ID: POL-06
TITLE: Limitation of Liability Policy
CATEGORY: Liability
EFFECTIVE DATE: 2024-01-01
OWNER: Legal Department

1. PURPOSE
This policy establishes acceptable standards for liability caps and exclusions in company contracts.

2. REQUIREMENTS
2.1 A counterparty's total liability under a contract should not be capped below an amount equal to twelve (12) months of fees paid or payable under the agreement, except where a lower cap is separately approved by the General Counsel.
2.2 Exclusions of liability for gross negligence, willful misconduct, or breach of confidentiality obligations are not acceptable and must be carved out of any liability cap or exclusion clause.
2.3 Uncapped liability is required for breaches of data protection obligations resulting in a reportable data breach.
2.4 Any mutual liability cap must apply equally to both parties unless a business justification for asymmetry is documented and approved.

3. APPLICABILITY
Applies to all commercial contracts where the company is a counterparty, particularly vendor, software licensing, and services agreements.

POLICY ID: POL-16
TITLE: Exclusivity and Most-Favored-Nation Policy
CATEGORY: Exclusivity

OWNER: Legal Department

1. PURPOSE
This policy governs the use of exclusivity and most-favored-nation (MFN) provisions in company contracts.

2. REQUIREMENTS
2.1 Exclusivity commitments binding the company to a single vendor or partner must not exceed a duration of twenty-four (24) months without Executive Committee approval.
2.2 Most-favored-nation clauses requiring a vendor to offer the company terms no less favorable than those offered to other customers require Legal Department review prior to acceptance.
2.3 Exclusivity provisions must include defined performance thresholds that, if unmet by the counterparty, permit the company to terminate the exclusivity without penalty.
2.4 Category-wide exclusivity (restricting the company from engaging any competing vendor in an entire product category) is discouraged and requires General Counsel sign-off.

3. APPLICABILITY
Applies to vendor, supply, and strategic partnership agreements.

POLICY ID: POL-12
TITLE: Dispute Resolution and Governing Law Policy
CATEGORY: Dispute Resolution
EFFECTIVE DATE: 2024-01-01
OWNER: Legal Department

1. PURPOSE
This policy establishes the company's preferred approach to dispute resolution and governing law provisions in contracts.

2. REQUIREMENTS
2.1 Contracts should specify a governing law consistent with the company's principal place of business, unless a different jurisdiction is required by the counterparty's regulatory environment and approved by Legal.
2.2 Mandatory binding arbitration clauses that waive the company's right to seek injunctive relief in court are not acceptable, except where injunctive relief remains expressly available as a carve-out.
2.3 Dispute resolution clauses should require a good-faith negotiation period of no less than thirty (30) days prior to initiation of formal proceedings.
2.4 Venue for any litigation or arbitration should be reasonably convenient and must not be unilaterally set solely at the counterparty's home jurisdiction without justification.

3. APPLICABILITY
Applies to all commercial contracts entered into by the company.

1. PURPOSE

Applies to vendor, supply, and strategic partnership agreements.

1. PURPOSE

POLICY ID: POL-14
TITLE: Auto-Renewal and Contract Renewal Policy
CATEGORY: Renewal
EFFECTIVE DATE: 2024-01-01
OWNER: Procurement Department

1. PURPOSE
This policy governs the use of automatic renewal provisions in company contracts.

2. REQUIREMENTS
2.1 Any contract with an automatic renewal clause must not require the company to give notice of non-renewal more than sixty (60) calendar days before the renewal date.
2.2 Automatic renewal terms must not increase contract value by more than five percent (5%) per renewal period without prior Finance Department approval.
2.3 Contracts with automatic renewal clauses must include the renewal date and notice deadline in a clearly identifiable, non-buried section of the agreement.
2.4 Multi-year automatic renewal commitments (renewal terms exceeding twelve months) require Director-level approval before signature.

3. APPLICABILITY
Applies to all subscription, licensing, and service contracts containing automatic renewal provisions.

policy_text:
POLICY ID: POL-05
TITLE: Contract Termination and Notice Policy
CATEGORY: Termination
EFFECTIVE DATE: 2024-01-01
OWNER: Legal Department

1. PURPOSE
This policy defines minimum notice periods required for termination of company contracts across categories.

2. REQUIREMENTS
2.1 Termination for convenience (without cause) requires a minimum notice period of thirty (30) calendar days, unless a longer period is specified by a category-specific policy (e.g., critical vendors require 60 days per POL-01).
2.2 Termination for cause requires a cure period of no less than fifteen (15) calendar days following written notice of the breach, except in cases of material data security breaches, which may permit immediate termination.
2.3 All termination notices must be delivered in writing to a designated notice address specified in the contract.
2.4 Contracts must not permit unilateral termination by a counterparty with less than fifteen (15) days notice under any circumstance.

3. APPLICABILITY
Applies to all commercial contracts entered into by the company, unless superseded by a more specific policy for a given contract category.

POLICY ID: POL-06
TITLE: Limitation of Liability Policy
CATEGORY: Liability
EFFECTIVE DATE: 2024-01-01
OWNER: Legal Department

1. PURPOSE
This policy establishes acceptable standards for liability caps and exclusions in company contracts.

2. REQUIREMENTS
2.1 A counterparty's total liability under a contract should not be capped below an amount equal to twelve (12) months of fees paid or payable under the agreement, except where a lower cap is separately approved by the General Counsel.
2.2 Exclusions of liability for gross negligence, willful misconduct, or breach of confidentiality obligations are not acceptable and must be carved out of any liability cap or exclusion clause.
2.3 Uncapped liability is required for breaches of data protection obligations resulting in a reportable data breach.
2.4 Any mutual liability cap must apply equally to both parties unless a business justification for asymmetry is documented and approved.

3. APPLICABILITY
Applies to all commercial contracts where the company is a counterparty, particularly vendor, software licensing, and services agreements.

POLICY ID: POL-17
TITLE: Warranty Policy
CATEGORY: Warranty
EFFECTIVE DATE: 2024-01-01
OWNER: Legal Department

1. PURPOSE
This policy defines minimum warranty standards required in vendor and supplier contracts.

2. REQUIREMENTS
2.1 Software and service vendors must provide a minimum warranty period of ninety (90) days from delivery or go-live, during which defects must be remedied at no additional cost.
2.2 Vendors must warrant that delivered products/services do not infringe upon the intellectual property rights of any third party.
2.3 Disclaimers of implied warranties (e.g., merchantability, fitness for purpose) must be reviewed and approved by Legal before acceptance, and should not eliminate express warranties negotiated in the agreement.
2.4 Warranty remedies should include, at minimum, repair, replacement, or refund at the company's option.

3. APPLICABILITY
Applies to all agreements involving the purchase or licensing of goods, software, or services by the company.
